title: Deputy Secretary Landau’s Meeting with Ugandan Foreign Minister Ayebare
summary_raw:
Office of the Spokesperson
Readout


			
			


			
			
August 28, 2026

The below is attributable to Spokesman Tommy Pigott:
Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau met today in Washington, D.C., with Ugandan Foreign Minister Adonia Ayebare. They discussed ways to advance bilateral cooperation on key issues, including shared global health priorities, economic growth, and regional security.

title: Statement from Assistant Secretary Dylan Johnson on Revoking Visa from Iraqi National on FBI Terror Watchlist Given Award by Previous Administration
summary_raw:
Office of the Spokesperson
Media Note


			
			


			
			
August 28, 2026

The U.S. Department of State has revoked the visa of an Iraqi national who was presented an award by the Biden Administration for her purported role in fighting corruption and her advocacy for “gender equity.”
Taif Sami Mohammed Al Shakarchi was given the International Woman of Courage Award in 2022 by former Secretary of State Anthony Blinken and former First Lady Jill Biden.
The award recognized “women from around the globe who have demonstrated exceptional courage, strength, and leadership in advocating for peace, justice, human rights, gender equity and equality, and the empowerment of women and girls, in all their diversity.”
This Iraqi national’s visa has now been revoked by the State Department following her placement on the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Terror Watchlist. She is no longer present in the United States.
Under President Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, suspected terrorists will never be allowed to remain in the United States.

title: U.S. Sanctions Sever Financial Lifelines of Iranian Regime
summary_raw:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesperson
Press Statement


			
			


			
			
August 28, 2026
Operation Economic Outcast continues in full force. Today, the United States is imposing sanctions on the manager of the Dubai branch of Iran’s Bank Melli, Reza Mohammad Taeedi. Bank Melli has served as a critical financial hub for Iran’s armed forces, including the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force and the Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics, both U.S.-sanctioned entities. We are also sanctioning a Hong Kong-based company that has helped designated Iranian individuals and entities to access the international financial system. In addition, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) proposed a rule that would revoke Banque Misr UAE’s correspondent banking access to U.S. financial institutions. Treasury assesses that Banque Misr UAE is a critical node for the Iranian regime’s access to U.S. dollars.
Today’s action intensifies our pressure campaign against Iran. As the regime prioritizes its malign activities above the needs of its people, we will sever the economic lifelines sustaining it. We will target individuals and entities that engage in illicit financial practices on behalf of the Iranian regime, including those working for Iranian banks outside the country.
Today’s sanctions actions are being taken pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, a counterterrorism authority, and E.O. 13902, which targets persons operating in Iran’s financial sector. FinCEN proposed its rule pursuant to section 311 of the USA PATRIOT Act. For more information on today’s action, please see the Department of the Treasury’s press release.

title: Deputy Secretary Landau Travels to Palau, the Federated States of Micronesia, Solomon Islands, and Kiribati
summary_raw:
Office of the Spokesperson
Media Note


			
			


			
			
August 28, 2026
Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau will travel to Palau, the Federated States of Micronesia (FSM), Solomon Islands, and Kiribati from August 31 to September 11. In Palau, the Deputy Secretary will participate in the Pacific Islands Forum (PIF) Leaders’ Meeting with Forum Dialogue Partners to strengthen ties between the United States and Pacific Islands governments. In FSM and Solomon Islands, he will meet with government representatives and business leaders to further advance our shared economic and security priorities. In Kiribati, he will attend the Kiribati Development Partners Forum and meet with government representatives.
The Deputy Secretary will be joined on the trip to Palau, Federated States of Micronesia and Solomon Islands by U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) Commandant Admiral Kevin Lunday, in recognition of the key role the Coast Guard plays in advancing regional maritime security. He will also be joined in Palau at the PIF by other U.S. interagency partners, including U.S. Pacific Command Deputy Commander Lieutenant General George Rowell and U.S. Department of the Interior Assistant Secretary Bill Hague.
The Pacific region remains an enduring foreign policy priority for the United States. The United States has deep and long-standing ties to the countries in the Pacific, who are not only our neighbors but also our friends. The United States is committed to engaging our Pacific Island partners to preserve an open, secure, and prosperous Pacific region.
